name: SC-03
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strongly Republican district with a -21 point partisan lean
Incumbent Sheri Biggs has a dominant fundraising edge ($505K to $41K)
No public polling and no expert ratings, but prediction markets price Democratic chances near 3%
model.rationale: This northwestern South Carolina seat leans heavily Republican, and first-term incumbent Sheri Biggs holds an overwhelming financial advantage over Democrat Eunice Lehmacher, who has raised under $41,000. With no polling or expert ratings suggesting vulnerability and markets pricing a Democratic win at roughly 3%, the fundamentals point to a comfortable Republican hold.
model.watch: Any unexpected scandal or major outside spending against Biggs would be the main route to a closer race, though a Democratic upset remains very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
South Carolina's 3rd District is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the state, with a partisan lean of about 21 points toward the GOP. First-term Republican incumbent Sheri Biggs is seeking reelection and holds a decisive financial advantage, having raised roughly twelve times more than Democratic challenger Eunice Lehmacher, whose campaign has about $18,000 on hand. A Libertarian candidate is also on the ballot but has shown little fundraising activity.

No public general-election polling or expert race ratings are available for this contest, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the incumbency advantage, and the money gap. Prediction markets give Democrats only a small chance of an upset. All available evidence points to Biggs being strongly favored to hold the seat in November.
